title: Using BossDB Tools to Access, Visualize, and Share Volumetric Neuroscience Data
author: Martinez, Guittari, et al.
materials: Python ≥3.8, with packages matplotlib and intern installed

steps.title: Browse public datasets and record identifiers
steps.instruction: Open each BossDB project page, locate and copy the collection, experiment, and channel identifiers, as well as the Neuroglancer link and URI; verify every alphanumeric value for accuracy before proceeding.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to the project page in a web browser.
Copy the collection ID, experiment ID, channel ID, Neuroglancer link, and URI.
Paste the values into a notebook or text file for later use.

steps.title: Access data with Python SDK
steps.instruction: Create a stable Python environment with the required intern package versions, configure the API token, and request a test subvolume using exact collection/experiment/channel strings; remember that intern expects Z‑Y‑X coordinate ordering and choose a region near the dataset centre.

substeps.instruction: Install the intern SDK (e.g., pip install intern) in a clean virtual environment.
Add your API token to the intern configuration (intern.cfg).
Specify the collection, experiment, and channel identifiers exactly as recorded.
Select a subvolume near the centre of the dataset to avoid padded edges.
Provide coordinates in ZYX order when calling intern.cutout.

steps.title: Retrieve data via Data API
steps.instruction: Build a cutout request to the data API using the same identifiers, ensure start and end coordinates are within dataset bounds, and include the correct Authorization header for private datasets before sending the request.

substeps.instruction: Form the request URL: https://api.bossdb.io/v1/... with collection/experiment/channel.
Set start and end coordinates that do not exceed the dataset limits.
Add an HTTP header: Authorization: Bearer <your_token> (required for private data).
Send the request (e.g., using curl or requests) and retrieve the image data.

steps.title: Query dataset metadata via API
steps.instruction: Compose a metadata query that includes all required fields such as voxel size, imaging modality, and species, using the correct schema definition, then submit the query and verify the response.

substeps.instruction: Create a JSON payload containing voxel size, imaging modality, species, and any other required fields.
Select the appropriate schema version for the dataset.
POST the payload to the metadata endpoint (e.g., https://api.bossdb.io/v1/metadata).
Check the returned status and data for successful validation.

steps.title: Create Neuroglancer visualization
steps.instruction: Modify the dataset URI by removing the leading “bossdb://” and replacing it with “boss://https://api.bossdb.io/”, then open the resulting Neuroglancer URL in a browser with a stable high‑bandwidth connection to ensure full loading of downsampled chunks.

substeps.instruction: Take the original URI (e.g., bossdb://mycollection/experiment/channel).
Replace the prefix with boss://https://api.bossdb.io/ to form the Neuroglancer link.
Paste the new link into a web browser.
Confirm that the connection is fast enough for streaming data.

steps.title: Create BossDB account and token
steps.instruction: Register for a BossDB account, generate an API token, store the token securely (do not share), and note that compromised tokens can be regenerated.

substeps.instruction: Sign up on the BossDB website.
Navigate to the token management page and create a new token.
Copy the token to a secure location (e.g., password manager).
If the token is ever exposed or expires, regenerate a new one.

steps.title: Upload public dataset with metadata
steps.instruction: Prepare the dataset in a supported format, assemble complete metadata including acquisition parameters and voxel units, and submit the upload; for datasets larger than 50 GB, coordinate with the BossDB team before ingestion.

substeps.instruction: Convert raw data to a supported format (e.g., N5, Zarr).
Create a metadata file containing voxel size, units, acquisition details, etc.
Use the public upload portal or API to submit the data and metadata.
If the total size exceeds 50 GB, email the BossDB team to arrange ingestion.

steps.title: Upload private small dataset
steps.instruction: Choose a unique URI such as “bossdb://username/test/images”, specify voxel size, shape, and units accurately when creating the dataset, place the API token in the intern.cfg file, and upload the dataset using the intern SDK.

substeps.instruction: Define a unique URI (e.g., bossdb://johnDoe/test/images).
When creating the dataset, enter the correct voxel dimensions, shape, and unit strings.
Edit intern.cfg to include your private token.
Use intern's upload functions to send the small dataset to BossDB.
